chunks: 2. My father (may Allah have mercy on him) said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us, who said: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa narrated from al-Hasan ibn 'Ali al-Khazzaz, from Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him) who said:

Verily, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) on the Day of Resurrection will be holding Allah's Waistband, and we will be holding the Prophet's Waistband, and our Shi'ites will be holding our Waistband. Then he said: And the Waistband is the Light.

key_terms.النُّورُ: The Light; referring to divine light or spiritual reality
key_terms.حُجْزَة: Waistband; a metaphor for holding onto authority or spiritual connection

ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of holding the Waistband (Hujzah) on the Day of Resurrection in Shia theology?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq presents this hadith to illustrate the metaphysical hierarchy of authority (wilayah) on the Day of Resurrection, where the Prophet holds Allah's waistband and the Imams hold the Prophet's, culminating in the faithful holding the Imams'. The Imam's clarification that 'hujzah' signifies divine Light (Nur) aligns with Shia exegetical traditions that interpret this as the tangible manifestation of spiritual guidance and proximity to God, distinguishing the Shi'ites as the true inheritors of this light.

en.sayed-ali-raza-rizvi: 2. My father (RA) that Sa`d ibn `Abd Allah said: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn `Isa said on the authority of al-Hasan ibn `Ali al-Khazzaz, that Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (AS) said:

“Verily, the Messenger of Allah (SA) will take hold of Allah’s Waistband [hujzah]. We will grab the Prophet’s Waistband and our Shi`ites will take hold of our Waistband.” He then said: “the Waistband is the Light [al-nur].”
